paras: The attempted lynching in Washington, Louisiana, was a crowd's threat to lynch an unnamed Black man on the night of Saturday, August 18, 1900, after he allegedly fired at a constable trying to arrest him. Sheriff Swords took him to the Opelousas jail, and two local white papers disagreed over how near the crowd came to lynching him.
Constable Philip Zernott held a warrant for the man, who was described as wanted in New Iberia; the Opelousas Courier added that he was said to be wanted there for criminal assault.

At about 9:30 p.m., during a political meeting, Zernott told the man of the warrant, and by both accounts he drew a pistol and fired at close range. Zernott, City Marshal John Lear and Sam Plonsky grappled with him, Plonsky beating him on the head with a stick, and a crowd from the meeting soon raised cries of lynching.

A telegram to the New Orleans Times-Democrat said a mob of about sixty was "determined to lynch the negro" and that the sheriff held it back with a revolver. In that account the sheriff, District Attorney Garland and others guarded the prisoner in a saloon, then rushed him out the rear and on to the Opelousas jail by about midnight.
The Washington Enterprise said the prisoner was held "to await orders from Iberia" and that the excitement died away within a few hours; the coverage does not name him or report his fate.

The Opelousas Courier ran the story on August 25 with the Times-Democrat telegram, as a narrow escape from a mob. The Washington Enterprise ran its account under the headline "Resisted Arrest," reprinted by the Weekly Iberian of New Iberia on September 1, and called the townspeople "very calm." No Black-press report appears in the coverage.

The Enterprise called the story that Sheriff Swords "kept them at bay at the point of a pistol" an "unfounded" rumor, contradicting the Times-Democrat telegram. The Enterprise was the town's own paper, closer to the scene but with a stake in its name.

reader.title: Attempted lynching in Washington, Louisiana
bases: A crowd raised cries of lynching against a Black prisoner after an arrest, and one report describes a mob of about sixty 'determined to lynch' him that the sheriff held back (A1, A2).

The prisoner was not killed; he was handed to the sheriff and jailed in Opelousas (A1, A2). The crowd's threat was extralegal and tied to his alleged shooting at a constable, so this was at most an attempted lynching, and A2 disputes even how serious the attempt was.

Two independent reports agree on the shooting at the constable, the arrest, the lynching threat and the removal to Opelousas, but the Washington Enterprise (A2) calls the account of a desperate mob held at pistol point, as given in A1, an 'unfounded' rumor.

accounts.label: Times-Democrat telegram (via Opelousas Courier)
accounts.gist: A mob of about sixty set on lynching the prisoner was held back by Sheriff Swords at revolver point; officials ringed him in a saloon, then rushed him out the rear through a broken fence and on to the Opelousas jail.

accounts.label: Washington Enterprise (via Weekly Iberian)
accounts.gist: Cries of lynching arose, but older citizens had the man turned over to the sheriff; the story of a desperate crowd held at pistol point was 'unfounded' and the excitement died away within hours.

framing.detail: The Opelousas Courier told the story as a dramatic rescue by the sheriff and officials, under a garbled headline, without comment on the mob.

Under the headline 'Resisted Arrest', the Washington Enterprise played down the lynching threat and praised local citizens as 'very calm', while reporting the beating with a stick as part of a justified arrest.

versions.value: A mob of about sixty 'determined to lynch' grew 'more furious'; the sheriff held it back with a revolver and had to rush the prisoner out the rear of a saloon
Cries of lynching arose but citizens were 'very calm'; the pistol standoff was an 'unfounded' rumor

conflicts.note: A1 relays a telegram sent from Opelousas; A2 is the Washington town paper, closer to the scene but with a stake in the town's reputation. Neither can be preferred on the evidence.

versions.value: Said to be wanted in New Iberia for criminal assault
Wanted in New Iberia (no charge named)

conflicts.note: The criminal assault charge appears only as hearsay in A1.

record_check.dossier: 1: the prisoner was beaten on the head with a stick during the arrest
No seizure from custody; a crowd threatened the prisoner while officers guarded him (per A1 at a saloon), which A2 disputes; beating during the arrest

record_check.record: accused of criminal assault (said to be wanted in New Iberia)
record_check.dossier: Accused of firing at a constable while resisting arrest; the criminal assault charge is only 'said' in A1, and A2 says only 'wanted in New Iberia'

record_check.record: warrant of arrest for criminal assault; resisted arrest and fired at the constable
record_check.dossier: The warrant's charge is not stated; the crowd's grievance was the shot fired at the constable
County not named in the reports; prisoner taken to the Opelousas jail

record_check.record: A crowd of about sixty tried to lynch ... sheriff held the crowd back
record_check.dossier: This is the Times-Democrat telegram's version only; the Washington Enterprise calls it an unfounded rumor

info: Saturday night, 18 August 1900 ('last Saturday' in the Courier of 25 August; about 9:30 p.m. per the Enterprise)
Washington, Louisiana, at the corner of Main and Dejean streets, during a political meeting
One unnamed Black man ('a burly negro')
Accused of resisting arrest and firing a pistol at Constable Philip Zernott; A1 says it was 'said' he was wanted in New Iberia for criminal assault, A2 says only that he was wanted in New Iberia
An unnamed crowd of white townspeople (race not stated) that gathered at the scene
Sheriff Swords took the prisoner to the Opelousas jail, where he arrived about midnight, to await orders from Iberia

sources.note: Local report plus N.O. Times-Democrat telegram of the 20th: unnamed Black man fired at constable Zernott; mob of about sixty 'determined to lynch'; Sheriff Swords held it back with a revolver and jailed the prisoner in Opelousas.
quotes: A mob of about sixty determined to lynch the negro, but the sheriff, with revolver in hand, held the crowd back
It is said the negro is wanted in New Iberia for criminal assault.
